en.headline: Acting housing chief says Wang Fuk Court site future may take years
en.dek: Michael Wong said consolidating ownership and demolishing the fire-damaged buildings will take years, with the site planned for community facilities or a park after recovery.
body: Acting Secretary for Housing Michael Wong said on Saturday that finalising the long-term future of the Wang Fuk Court site in Tai Po could take years.
Wong, who is also Deputy Financial Secretary, spoke on Commercial Radio two days after the first anniversary of the November 2025 fire that killed 168 people and destroyed most of the estate.

The government has said the recovered land will not be used for redevelopment or profit but for community facilities or a park. Wong said consolidating ownership rights and the eventual demolition of the buildings would require time and would be carried out over the coming years.

He added that the specific nature of any park and associated community facilities would be discussed with the community in the years ahead. When asked about a possible memorial park similar to those after other disasters, Wong said he would not speculate on details at this stage because the matter required consideration of stakeholders' feelings and involved land planning and design.
Correction: The Chinese version previously misspelled the name of Michael Wong; it has been corrected.

zh.headline: 署理房屋局長稱廣福邨用地未來用途或需數年決定
zh.dek: 黃偉綸表示整合業權及清拆火警損毀樓宇需時，用地收回後計劃作社區設施或公園用途。
body: 署理房屋局長黃偉綸周六表示，大埔廣福邨用地的長遠未來或需數年才能最終決定。
黃偉綸同時是財政司副司長，他在商業電台節目中發言，距離2025年11月導致168人死亡的廣福邨大火一周年僅兩日。
政府已表明收回土地後不會用於重建或牟利，而會作社區設施或公園用途。黃偉綸說，整合業權及最終清拆樓宇都需要時間，相關程序將在未來數年進行。
他補充，公園及相關社區設施的具體性質，未來數年會有機會與社區討論。被問及會否興建類似其他災難後的紀念公園時，黃偉綸表示現階段不會推測細節，因為這是嚴肅事情，需考慮各持份者感受，並涉及土地規劃及公園設計。
更正：中文版本先前誤將姓名寫錯，現已更正。
